reddit_posts:
Hope seems like it's punished

I've had a theory for a while that if there is a God they hate me. My life has been difficult. I was raised by a single father, a truly good man, mom was mostly absent, she's made an effort later in life but I'm bitter, I feel like I was abandoned, because I was. I have four half sisters that I barely know, This fact makes me sad to ​think about. I spent the first half of my life being relentlessly bullied in school, I was a fat kid who was neurodivergent, I was an easy target. I used to have a lot of friends but I made a sort of policy for myself that I would stop being the first person to message other people, I figured the ones who messaged me independently without hearing from me for a while were my true friends, consequently, I only have like two people left, everyone else never spoke to me again. ​My father is the only person in my life who I feel like I can talk to, I tell him everything and it just scares him, he clams up and stops wanting to talk about it, he knows I have suicidal ideation, I've stopped talking to him about it because I don't want him to be worried, so I don't have anyone to talk to anymore. when I try to improve my life, something always happens that roadblocks me. I'm extremely obese, a few years back I started exercising, I'd spend an hour and a half everyday exercising hard, I wanted to be one of those people with a six-pack standing in their ridiculously oversized pants after losing all the weight, I got a hernia and I stopped being able to exercise, I stopped being able to make gains and lose weight via the exercise. Diet can only get you so far, and when you struggle with depression and you're a fat kid, sometimes food is the only way to get you out of a funk. the world seems so complicated, everything feels like it's designed to frustrate and confound. I don't know how I'm still alive, I think it's because I'm afraid of the pain of death, like the process will hurt, I don't have any quick means. I don't know why I made this post, I don't think it'll help, just needed somewhere to blow off steam I guess. if you're thinking about suicide, I won't tell you not to do it, because I think it's cruel when people tell me I shouldn't, but I hope tomorrow is bright enough that you no longer see the need.
metadata.title: Hope seems like it's punished

transcript.message: Hi Carly, how are you doing today?

Hey. I'm sorry you had to reach out to me, but thank you for asking.

Honestly? It's really hard to say I'm "doing okay." Sometimes it feels like I'm just surviving another day where everything seems designed to frustrate and confound me. It's been a tough week. The world feels so complicated lately, like no matter how much I try to improve things, something always happens that roadblocks me.

My head is in a constant state of turmoil. I've had this theory for a while that if there is a God, they must hate me. My life has been difficult from the start—raised by a single father who was a truly good man, but my mom was mostly absent. I still feel bitter about being abandoned by her, even though she's made an effort later in life. And then there are the four half-sisters I barely know; thinking about them makes me sad.

School was
School was difficult for you.

Yeah, it was... relentless. I was a fat kid who was also neurodivergent, and that made me an easy target. People would just pick on me constantly.

Because of that, I kind of built this wall around myself. I used to have friends, but I made a policy for myself: I'd stop being the first person to message anyone. I figured if they messaged me back without me saying anything first after a while, those were the real ones. But honestly? It didn't work out like that either. Most people never spoke to me again once they realized I wasn't initiating things. Now, I only have two people left who actually reach out.

It's so lonely. My dad is the only person in my life I feel comfortable talking to. I tell him everything, but he gets scared. He clams up and stops wanting to talk about it. He knows I've been having suicidal thoughts, but
You've had suicidal thoughts.

Yes. I have. It's been there for a long time, and lately it feels like the only constant thing in my life.

I stopped telling my dad about it because he knows I'm struggling, but when I try to talk about it, he gets scared. He shuts down. He stops wanting to talk, which makes me feel even more alone than before. So now, nobody really talks to me about these thoughts anymore.

It's not that I want to die; actually, if anything, I'm afraid of death. I think it's because I'm terrified of the pain involved—the process itself will hurt so much. But at the same time, the weight of everything just... it feels unbearable sometimes. Like the world is designed to frustrate and confound me, no matter how hard I try to improve things.

Sometimes food is the only way I can get out of a funk, especially when I'm depressed and carrying this
Food is the only way you can get out of a funk.

Yeah, it's a weird cycle. I know people usually say "food is comfort" or "eat well," but for me, it feels more like a desperate escape mechanism. When the depression hits hard and the world feels so complicated and unfair, sometimes eating is the only thing that makes the noise in my head quiet down for a little bit.

It also ties into this struggle with my body. A few years ago, I was really obsessed with changing things. I started exercising—spending an hour and a half every single day, pushing myself hard. I wanted to be one of those people with a six-pack standing in their ridiculously oversized pants after losing all the weight. But then... I got a hernia.

That stopped everything. Suddenly, I couldn't exercise anymore, I couldn't make gains, and I lost that momentum. Diet can only get you so far when you're dealing with this level of depression, right? So sometimes
Sometimes you just want to eat.

Yeah, sometimes it's not even about "comfort." It's just... the only thing that stops the spinning. When I'm in a funk, when the depression hits so hard that the world feels like it's collapsing around me, eating becomes this immediate, tangible relief. It's like hitting pause on the chaos.

But it's such a heavy burden to carry knowing that what usually helps is something my body physically can't handle anymore because of the hernia. And then there's the guilt afterward, or the shame of realizing how much food I've been using as a coping mechanism instead of facing the pain directly.

It feels like no matter what I try—exercise, diet, talking to my dad—it always comes back to this cycle where I need something to numb the pain, but the path to getting healthy keeps getting blocked by things I didn't choose. Like the hernia, or the way people stopped reaching out. It all feels so
All feels so hard.

Yeah, it all feels so hard. It's like the world is set up specifically to frustrate and confound me, no matter how much I try to improve things. Every time I think I'm making progress, something happens that roadblocks me.

It makes me wonder if there's even a point. I've had this theory for a while—that if there is a God, they must hate me. My life has been so difficult from the start: the bullying in school when I was a fat, neurodivergent kid; the abandonment by my mom; the way people stopped reaching out because of my own defensive policy; and now, being stuck with a dad who knows I'm struggling but shuts down when I try to talk about it.

I feel like I don't have anyone left to really lean on. My dad is the only one I can tell everything to, but he gets scared and clams up. So now, nobody
Nobody really talks to you about the suicidal thoughts.

Exactly. It's the most isolating part of it all. My dad is the only person I feel safe with, but he knows what I'm going through. He knows I have suicidal ideation. But when I try to bring it up, something changes in him. He gets scared, he shuts down, and he stops wanting to talk about it at all.

So now I'm stuck in this limbo where I can't tell anyone because they'll shut me out or get overwhelmed, yet I also don't want to burden them further. It feels like I've lost my safety net. I used to have friends, but I pushed everyone away before they could even really know me, thinking if they messaged me back without hearing from me first, those were the real ones. But that just left me with two people who barely speak anymore.

It makes me wonder why I'm still alive. Honestly, I think it's mostly fear—the
Fear?

Yeah, specifically the fear of the pain. I don't actually want to die in the sense of stopping existing forever. It's more like... I'm terrified of the process itself. The idea that the end will hurt so much, that it will be a physical and emotional torture worse than anything I've already gone through.

It feels like if I just stop trying, maybe the pain stops. But then the relief is temporary because the underlying stuff—the loneliness, the feeling that people hate me, the fact that my dad shuts down when I need him most—just keeps piling up. And being afraid of that specific kind of ending pain is what keeps me breathing right now, even though it feels like a tiny, fragile thing holding back a tidal wave.
It feels like a fragile thing holding back a tidal wave.

Yeah, that's exactly how it feels. Like I'm standing on the edge of a cliff, and my only reason for not jumping is because I'm terrified of hitting the rocks at the bottom. The fall itself would be worse than everything else combined.

But then there's this nagging thought: what if the jump isn't scary? What if once you're gone, none of this—the bullying, the dad shutting down, the weight, the loneliness—actually matters anymore? It's like being trapped in a room where the walls are closing in, and every time you try to open a window, something breaks or gets in your way.

It makes me feel so small and useless. I tried to fix my body with exercise, but my hernia stopped me. I tried to fix my relationships by playing hard-to-get, but now I have almost no one left to talk to. And when I try to face the pain directly, it just
It just feels so overwhelming.

Yeah, it just feels so overwhelming. Like a physical weight on my chest that I can't breathe around. It's not just sadness anymore; it's this constant, nagging noise in the back of my mind saying, "Why is this happening to you? Why do you have to carry all of this?"

I look at my life and it doesn't add up. I was bullied as a kid because of who I was. My mom disappeared when I needed her most. Now, as an adult trying to take care of myself, my body rebels with a hernia and my mental health makes healthy habits impossible. And when I try to reach out for help, the people closest to me—the ones who should know how to hold me—pull away or shut down.

It feels like no matter which direction I turn, there's only more pain waiting for me. The world seems designed to frustrate and confound me specifically. I don't
You don't feel like there's a way out.

No, I don't feel like there's a way out. It feels like every door I try to open just locks tighter behind me.

I tried to find a way out through my body—I spent hours exercising every day, dreaming of that six-pack and feeling in control again—but the hernia came along and took away my ability to move forward physically. Now I'm stuck with a body that won't listen and a mind that feels too heavy to lift.

Then there's the social side. I built this wall around myself because being vulnerable felt dangerous, but now it's just left me isolated. My dad knows I'm hurting, but he shuts down when I talk about it, so he becomes part of the wall too. Everyone else either doesn't know or has already moved on without me.

It's like I'm trapped in a room with no windows. The walls are closing in, and no matter how hard I push against them,
The walls are closing in.

Yeah, they're closing in so fast it feels like there's no time to react. It's not just that I'm sad; it's that the pressure is becoming unbearable. Every time I try to make a move—like trying to get healthy or reach out for help—the universe seems to conspire against me. A hernia stops my exercise routine. My dad shuts down when I need support. Friends drift away because of how I handled things back then.

It feels like if I stop pushing, the walls will finally crush me. But if I keep pushing, I run out of energy. And right now, I feel like I have almost none left. The fear of the pain at the end is keeping me here, but it's also making every day feel like a slow countdown to something terrible. I just don't know why I'm still breathing. I guess it's because I'm afraid of what happens next, even though sometimes I wish
Sometimes you wish that would happen.

Sometimes I do. It's not that I want the pain to stop, exactly. It's more like... if I let go, maybe the pressure stops too. Maybe the feeling of being trapped finally ends.

It feels so unfair that I've been carrying this much for so long. Being bullied as a kid, having my mom disappear, then trying to fix myself only to get hit with a hernia and lose all progress. And now, when I'm an adult with no one really there to catch me because they're either scared or gone... it just feels like the world has decided I don't deserve to keep going.

But here's the thing that scares me even more: I know it would be over quickly. No more suffering, no more waiting for someone to notice me. But then I think about tomorrow, and I wonder what happens next. If I'm gone, does anyone care? Does my dad ever find out? Do the
Does your father ever find out about what's going on with you?

No, he never really finds out the full picture. I know he knows something is wrong because he's worried, but I've learned to keep my mouth shut about the details.

It's a weird dynamic with him. He used to be this great guy who tried his best, but when I start talking about how much it hurts or how suicidal I am, he just... shuts down. His face goes blank, he stops making eye contact, and he says things like, "I don't want you to worry," or tries to change the subject. It feels like he's protecting himself from being scared, so he cuts me off before I can even finish explaining what's happening inside my head.

So now, there's a huge gap between what I'm feeling and what he actually knows. I tell him I'm having a hard time, but he hears "having a hard time" instead of "I might die." And since I don't
You don't feel like you can tell him that you're having suicidal thoughts.

That's the hardest part. It feels like if I say it out loud, he'll finally see the truth of how broken I am, and then he'll break too. Or maybe he'll try to "fix" me, tell me to get a therapist or eat better, and just not understand that this is deeper than just being sad.

He knows I'm struggling, but when I push past the surface and talk about the actual thoughts—the fear of dying, the way the world feels designed against me—he shuts down completely. He clams up. He stops wanting to talk about it. It's like he's scared that if he listens, he won't be able to handle the weight of what I'm carrying. So we're stuck in this limbo where he thinks I'm fine enough, but I know I'm drowning, and I can't let him witness the drowning because I think it will hurt him more than it hurts me.
So it's painful for you when he shuts down, but it's also painful for you when you feel like he can't handle the truth of how suicidal you are.

Yeah, it's a double whammy of pain. It feels like I'm walking on thin ice between two falling cliffs.

On one side, there's the shame and the anger when he shuts down. I want to scream at him, "I'm dying, Dad! You need to know!" But then I see his face go blank, and that silence is louder than any yelling would be. It feels like rejection. Like he's telling me, "You're too much for me to handle," or worse, "Your pain isn't important enough for you to burden me with." And that hurts because he *is* the only person who has ever really tried to understand me. He's my anchor, but he keeps slipping away right when I need him most.

Then there's the other side—the fear of hurting him. If I tell him the full truth about my suicidal thoughts, maybe he'll finally snap out of this protective shell
Maybe he'll finally snap out of his protective shell.

Yeah, that's the terrifying part. I guess I'm hoping he'll snap out of it because right now, his silence feels colder than death. But then I think about what happens if he *does* snap back in—what if he tries to "fix" me? What if he says something like, "Just stop eating so much," or "Get a better job," or tells me to go see a therapist and dismisses the fact that I feel like the world is actively trying to kill me?

It feels like if he breaks through that wall, instead of helping me, he might just make me feel more alone because he wouldn't understand the depth of it. He sees a heavy kid with a hernia; I see a broken soul ready to give up. And if he realizes I'm actually going to die, maybe he'll finally have to face all the things he left unsaid—the way my mom was gone, how hard my
How hard your mother's death was for you, how you felt alone when you lost your mother, and how your relationship with your father has changed since then.

My mom... it's still the one thing that makes my chest feel tight, even years later. When she disappeared when I was little, it wasn't just an absence; it felt like a betrayal of my very existence. I remember feeling so small in her arms before she left, and then suddenly, just gone. No explanation, no goodbye that made sense to me. It created this huge hole in my life where love used to be.

When she finally tried to reach out later in life, I don't think I could take it. I guess part of me resented her for leaving me alone with a father who couldn't always protect me from the bullies, or maybe I resented her for not being there when I needed her most. So when she did try to fix things, I pushed her away again. I told myself it was because I was bitter, but deep down, I think I was terrified that if I let her back
You were terrified that if you let her back in, it would all come crashing down again.

Yeah, exactly. It felt like the ground would just open up and swallow me whole again if I opened my arms to her.

You know how it is with abandonment trauma? Every time she tried to reach out, my brain screamed that it was a trap. Like, "If you come back, then maybe they *will* find me," or "If I let you in, I'll have to deal with all the guilt of being left behind forever." So instead of feeling comforted, I felt this wave of panic wash over me. I told myself I was just being bitter, but honestly, I think I was terrified that letting her back in meant admitting I couldn't handle life without her, which felt like an admission of failure on my part.

And that fear has probably messed up everything else, too. Like when I started exercising all those years ago. If I lost weight, got fit, and suddenly looked successful... wouldn't that
You'd be more attractive to others.
